column1: # Summary: audited §11.1-§11.5 against main HEAD 3cc63c55ed04df7035c1c06a8cc754e20a0b1ce1 using git show main:<file> blobs only.
# Scope parsed 136 PR table rows, including active rows, moved/deferred trace rows, and Block 5 sub-block rows. Output contains 253 TSV records:
# 206 cite/file records plus 47 NO_CITE PR rows. Status totals: VALID=56, STALE=40, OUT_OF_FILE=6, NEW_FILE_NOT_ON_MAIN=104, NO_CITE=47.
# Compared with CODEX1 baseline (23 valid / 39 stale / 3 out-of-file / 61 no-cite), raw valid count improved by +33 and all-record valid ratio rose
# from 18.3% to 22.1%. True line/file-record quality did not improve: VALID among cite/file records fell from 35.4% baseline to 27.2% because
# Phase 4 added many not-yet-on-main rows and several older stale anchors survived restructure. So answer is mixed: yes, more anchors are now
# verified; no, §11 is not cite-clean enough for autonomous dispatch without repair. Residual stale cites escaping fixes include PR #3
# handlers/terrain_checkpoints.py:97,102; #35 handlers/terrain_pipeline.py:992,999; #36 profile instance cites; #43 vegetation/procedural grass;
# #45 handlers/environment.py:2861; #62 water-depth cites; #65 dead-RNG cleanup cites; B5-U2/B5-U3/B5-U4 importer cites; B5-T1 visual QA; B5-A4
# asset-budget cites; and B5-DOC2 backfill cites. Phase 4 focus rows B5-U-NAV, B5-U15-U22, B5-C7-C12, B5-D5-D8, B5-T8-T10, and #65 are mostly
# NEW_FILE_NOT_ON_MAIN or no-line documentation; expected, but they need stronger caveats before agents treat them as main anchors. Highest-risk
# repair order: stale surgical-code rows first, then out-of-file rows, then Phase 4 NEW rows. Do not dispatch PR owners from rows marked STALE,
# OUT_OF_FILE, or NO_CITE unless the PR packet explicitly says the cite is historical/negative evidence rather than the edit target.
